The meters we installed transmitted intermittently on the 900 MHz range of frequencies, mostly known for garage door openers. Our meters have an FCC label on them designating them as class 1 devices. They are rated for this frequency, and have a range of about 1/4 mile. I've had to track down meters who's paperwork didn't match the serial number (installer error when entering the data) and had to search in a circular pattern to find the sister meter it was communicating with. They are actually very simple devices, there is not much contained within the plastic shell.

As for remote on/off switching, the residential meters I installed were not capable of it. If a property was not to have live electric at the service, we installed a preset open meter.

The benefits are a real time reading of demand, so the generating plant can compensate for peak. The value to the end customer is really unnoticeable in practical terms, but the power generating company can now be far more streamlined in it's production.
